messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:  
The test `shortTextFilesAreNoTARs()` fails because the `ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(InputStream)` method incorrectly identifies short text files (<= ~100 bytes) as tar archives. The bug report states that this undesired detection was introduced by the fix for COMPRESS-117.

Analyzing the main method `createArchiveInputStream(InputStream)` (lines 197-254), the factory tries to identify the archive type by reading signature bytes from the stream and matching them against various archive formats: Zip, Jar, Ar, Cpio, Dump, and finally Tar. For tar detection, it reads 512 bytes (one tar block) and calls `TarArchiveInputStream.matches(byte[], int)` (lines 231-238).

In the `TarArchiveInputStream.matches` method (lines 518-554), it checks for the tar magic number and version fields at specific offsets within the input bytes to verify the tar signature.

If the signature check passes, the factory immediately returns a new `TarArchiveInputStream`. In addition, the factory tries a further auto-recognition step introduced for COMPRESS-117 (lines 239-247) where it creates a `TarArchiveInputStream` from the initial 512-byte header and calls `getNextEntry()` on it to verify the stream looks like a tar archive before returning the real `TarArchiveInputStream`.

The problem seems to be that when the input is a very short text file (shorter than 512 bytes), the buffering and recognition behaves incorrectly: 

- The `TarArchiveInputStream.matches` might return true for some random text due to the magic number offsets possibly matching coincidentally in short inputs.
- During the `getNextEntry()` call inside the factory, the `TarArchiveInputStream` tries to read entries from an in-memory ByteArrayInputStream of the header bytes. Since this is a short text, this method likely doesn't fail or throws an exception as expected, allowing the factory to mistakenly conclude the stream is a tar archive.
- This incorrectly causes the factory to return a `TarArchiveInputStream` for short text files, failing the test which expects an `ArchiveException`.

Further details in `TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry()` (lines 172-238) show logic for reading tar record headers and entries, but since the input is a non-archive text of less than 512 bytes, this might result in undefined or lenient behavior that does not throw an exception during the inner `getNextEntry()` call in the factory.

In summary, the root cause lies in the overly lenient tar archive auto-detection logic introduced after reading 512 bytes and attempting to parse a tar entry. The heuristic incorrectly identifies short text files (<= 100 bytes) as tar archives, violating the contract expected by the test.

The fix area would be to improve the tar archive detection logic inside `ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream` and/or inside `TarArchiveInputStream.matches` and `getNextEntry()` so that short or invalid files do not pass the detection heuristic. Possibly also the additional parsing step inside the factory (lines 240-247) should be stricter in identifying valid tar archives.

This behavior matches the description in the bug report and explains the failing test outcome.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
